workforceModel.status: Digital and IT mature-team high-water model with a four-post permanent institutional core, 50/50 Product Manager allocation across Student and Staff Hubs, confirmed Year One architecture phasing, a rolling sandwich-year placement and unresolved specialist workforce sourcing
workforceModel.summary: The permanent institutional product core remains four Digital and IT posts: Product Manager, Backend Engineer, Full-Stack Developer and UX/UI Designer. Jon Ward has confirmed that the 1.0 FTE Product Manager should be funded 50/50 between the Student and Staff Hubs. James Costerton has clarified that Solution Architect / Technical Lead input should average 0.75 FTE in Year One, front-loaded from full-time input and tapering through 0.5 and 0.25 as the architecture settles. Later-year architecture capacity remains high-water until the enduring service model is agreed. A rolling paid sandwich-year engineering placement remains a recurrent development and talent-pipeline commitment. DevOps, D365 / Power Platform, Cloud Infrastructure and IAM remain specialist high-water capacity pending further validation. The D365 line is explicitly a contingency rather than a settled dedicated Hub role: James advises that the requirement is not yet defined and may be partly or wholly supplied by the core R&C CRM team once the MVP shape is clearer. Infuse QA remains outsourced non-pay testing. Mark Peace as Product Owner and the expected existing IT Delivery Manager remain existing capacity rather than funded appointments.
